People often just say "four." This one is a straight four,{se:04}{wait:00}but this one is just a four.{se:05}{wait:00}One with a gap in it, or with another stone at one end,{wait:00}or touching the edge of the board is not a straight four.{wait:00}

The board has 15 lines running across and 15 running down.{wait:00}The black dot in the center is called "tengen."{wait:00}

Five stones of the same color in an unbroken row.{wait:00}{se:01}Whoever makes a five first wins the game.{wait:00}White wins with five or more in a row,{wait:00}but Black wins only with exactly five.{wait:00}

Sometimes six stones end up in a row at once.{wait:00}{se:0F}This is called an "overline."{wait:00}An overline still wins for White,{wait:00}but for Black it is a forbidden move, so Black loses.{wait:00}

Three stones in a row.{wait:00}With the next move it can become a straight four.{wait:00}{se:10}In other words, a three is a straight four with one stone taken away.{wait:00}{se:11}A three can be defended like this.{wait:00}{se:12}For Black and White alike, once one end is blocked,{wait:00}{se:13}even if a four is made with the next move,{wait:00}{se:14}it gets blocked like this.{wait:00}A three is a straight four minus one stone,{wait:00}but playing threes one after another{wait:00}never wins the game if they get blocked.{wait:00}A three is a weak attack.{wait:00}
A three with a gap in it.{wait:00}If you put a stone in the gap,{wait:00}{se:16}it becomes a straight four.{wait:00}{se:17}But if it is blocked like this, it cannot become a straight four.{wait:00}

Four stones in a row.{wait:00}{se:18}When one end is blocked, as with Black, and it cannot win,{wait:00}it is called a "four."{wait:00}When both ends are open, as with White,{wait:00}so that even with one end blocked the next move is as good as a win,{wait:00}{se:19}it is called a "straight four." A four is a strong attack.{wait:00}
A four with a gap in it.{wait:00}{se:1A}Put a stone in the gap and it becomes a five.{wait:00}

Making a four and a three with a single move.{wait:00}{se:1B}Placing a stone like this makes a four and a three at once, which leads to a win.{wait:00}{se:1C}Even if the four of the four-three is blocked,{wait:00}{se:1D}the next move makes a straight four.{wait:00}The four-three is one way to win at renju.{wait:00}

A four-three in which the three became a four.{wait:00}One move makes two fours.{wait:00}{se:1E}White may play a double-four,{wait:00}but for Black it is a forbidden move and Black loses.{wait:00}Straight fours or plain fours, if Black makes two fours at once, Black loses.{wait:00}
Making two or more threes at once with a single move.{wait:00}{se:1F}White may make a double-three,{wait:00}but for Black it is a forbidden move and Black loses.{wait:00}

A three that cannot become a straight four on the next move.{wait:00}{se:20}Threes where, even with a stone added, one end is closed{wait:00}{se:21}so no straight four forms, or where the four would be an overline and lose by a foul,{wait:00}{se:22}are not real threes.{wait:00}

A four-three or double-three that includes a false three.{wait:00}Such a double-three is not a forbidden move.{wait:00}{se:23}It happens when stones are placed like this.{wait:00}At a glance it looks like a four-three-three or a double-three,{wait:00}but one of the threes is blocked, or lies on an overline.{wait:00}

The moves Black must not play.{wait:00}Double-threes, double-fours and overlines made with one move.{wait:00}{se:24}Black loses whether Black plays one or is forced into one.{wait:00}The rule was added to balance Black's first-move advantage.{wait:00}White can also win by trapping Black into a forbidden move.{wait:00}

Attacking moves.{wait:00}{se:25}Playing a three is called "hiku" (drawing).{wait:00}{se:26}Playing a four is called{wait:00}{se:30}"nobiru" (extending).{wait:00}{se:35}Playing a split three or a split four is called{wait:00}{se:36}"tobu" (jumping).{wait:00}{se:27}A move that sets up a four-three win next is called{wait:00}{se:28}"miseru" (showing).{wait:00}{se:29}A move that sets up a four-chase win next is called{wait:00}{se:2A}"fukumu" (containing). A four-chase win goes{wait:00}{se:2B}like this:{wait:00}{se:31}four,{wait:00}{se:32}four, four,{wait:00}{se:2C}and so on,{wait:00}{se:2D}until fours in a row end in a four-three win.{wait:00}{se:2E}White's move that forces Black into a foul is called "hameru" (trapping).{wait:00}{se:2F}White has trapped Black into a double-three foul.{wait:00}{se:34}This is how Black gets trapped while trying to stop White's five.{wait:00}
